1.overview: Paul and Sosthenes greet the Corinthian church, give thanks for its gifts and calling, and urge unity amid factions aligned with Paul, Apollos, Cephas, and Christ. Paul contrasts the world’s wisdom with the message of Christ crucified, which is God’s power and wisdom, and says that God’s choice of the lowly leaves no room for boasting except in the Lord.

sections.heading: God’s choice and the Lord’s boast

2.overview: Paul recalls proclaiming Jesus Christ crucified in weakness, relying on the Spirit’s power so the Corinthians’ faith rests on God rather than human wisdom. He contrasts the age’s wisdom with God’s hidden wisdom, revealed by the Spirit, and explains that spiritual truths are discerned by the Spirit and expressed by those who have the mind of Christ.

sections.heading: Paul’s Proclamation in the Spirit’s Power
Spiritual Discernment and the Mind of Christ

3.overview: Paul rebukes the Corinthians for their immaturity and factions, describing himself and Apollos as servants while God gives growth. He explains that Christ is the foundation on which builders’ work will be tested, warns against harming God’s temple and worldly wisdom, and concludes that all things belong to the Corinthians, who belong to Christ and God.

4.overview: Paul describes himself and Apollos as servants and stewards accountable to the Lord, who alone judges hidden motives. He contrasts the Corinthians’ pride with the apostles’ hardships, then warns them as their spiritual father and announces Timothy’s visit and his own possible return.

5.overview: Paul condemns the Corinthian church’s tolerance of a man living with his father’s wife and directs the assembled community to remove him, with the aim of his eventual salvation. He warns that sin spreads like leaven, links the church’s purity to Christ’s sacrifice as the Passover lamb, and distinguishes discipline of members from judgment of outsiders.

sections.heading: The incestuous man and church discipline

6.overview: Paul challenges the Corinthians for taking disputes between believers before unbelieving judges, arguing that they should be able to settle such matters within the church and should not wrong one another. He warns that the unrighteous will not inherit God’s kingdom, recalls the Corinthians’ transformation, and argues that their bodies belong to Christ and are temples of the Holy Spirit, so they must not be joined to sexual immorality.

sections.heading: The Unrighteous and the Corinthians’ Transformation
The Body, Christ, and Sexual Immorality

7.overview: Paul gives guidance on marital duties, separation, and marriage between believers and unbelievers, then urges each person to remain in the situation in which God called them. He discusses singleness and marriage amid the present crisis, the concerns of married and unmarried people, and decisions about betrothal and remarriage after a spouse’s death.

sections.heading: Singleness and marriage in the present crisis

8.overview: Paul addresses food sacrificed to idols, contrasting knowledge that puffs up with love that builds up and affirming that there is one God, the Father, and one Lord, Jesus Christ. He explains that eating is not inherently significant, but exercising freedom in a way that harms a believer with a weak conscience sins against Christ, so he resolves not to eat meat if it causes another to stumble.

9.overview: Paul defends his apostleship and the right of gospel workers to receive material support, while explaining that he gives up this right to avoid hindering the gospel. He describes adapting to different people to win some, then compares gospel service to athletic competition and says he disciplines himself to avoid disqualification.

sections.heading: Paul’s Apostleship and Right to Support

10.overview: Paul recalls Israel’s passage through the sea and wilderness provision, then cites their judgments as warnings against idolatry, immorality, testing Christ, and complaint, while affirming God’s faithfulness amid temptation. He argues that participation in the Lord’s table excludes fellowship with demons and instructs the Corinthians to use their freedom over food in ways that honor God and benefit others.

11.overview: Paul commends the Corinthians for keeping the traditions he delivered, then discusses head coverings in worship, grounding his instructions in headship, creation, mutual dependence, and church practice. He rebukes divisions and selfishness at the Lord’s Supper, recalls Jesus’ words over the bread and cup, and calls for self-examination, mutual waiting, and further instruction when he comes.

12.overview: Paul explains that spiritual gifts have diverse forms but come from the same Spirit and are given for the common good. He compares the church to one body with many interdependent members, then lists roles and gifts in the church and introduces the greater way he will describe next.

13.overview: Paul argues that speech, prophecy, knowledge, faith, and sacrifice have no value without love, then describes love’s qualities. He contrasts love’s permanence with the passing of partial gifts and concludes that faith, hope, and love remain, with love greatest.

14.overview: Paul contrasts tongues with prophecy, arguing that intelligible speech builds up the church and enables shared understanding. He sets rules for orderly worship, including how tongues and prophecy are used, and concludes that everything in the church must be done properly and in order.

15.overview: Paul recalls the gospel of Christ’s death and resurrection, cites its witnesses, and argues that Christ’s resurrection establishes the future resurrection of the dead. He describes the resurrection body and the final transformation in which death is defeated, then concludes that work in the Lord is not in vain.

16.overview: Paul instructs the Corinthians to set aside a weekly collection for the Jerusalem believers and outlines his travel plans, including his stay in Ephesus and possible visits from Timothy and Apollos. He gives final instructions about faithful service and love, acknowledges Stephanas, Fortunatus, and Achaicus, sends greetings, and closes with his own greeting and blessing.
